A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ODE-GS. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original extrapolation results on D-NeRF, NVFi and HyperNeRF, plus ablation, variational-model and multi-scene experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds training-variant experiments, temporal-degradation analyses, context/split evaluations and qualitative diagnostics.

M1.justification: v4 introduces evaluated training variants that add image L1+SSIM reprojection supervision or leave interpolation parameters trainable during extrapolation training (Section 4.4; Appendix B.2.2). The recommended two-stage architecture, latent dynamics, sampling strategy and regularizers remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight D-NeRF, ten NVFi and six HyperNeRF scenes, including the same held-out-whale generalization setting. Added analyses use existing scenes; altered context lengths and temporal splits change settings within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds 4D-Rotor-Gaussians to the D-NeRF comparison in Table 1. Figures 17–18 also newly compare the no-ODE Transformer directly with Deformable-GS. Comparator membership in the principal NVFi and HyperNeRF tables is retained.

E3.justification: The default benchmark splits, metrics, model sizes and training budgets remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce freezing and reprojection-supervision controls, while Table 11 evaluates bouncingballs with context span 0.1 instead of 0.6 across 65–95% training-time splits.

E4.justification: v4 substantially expands diagnostic coverage: reprojection supervision, joint interpolation/extrapolation training, temporal degradation, context/split sensitivity, no-ODE qualitative comparisons and an illustrated interpolation failure. The earlier component ablations, variational comparison and multi-scene experiment are retained, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and scene averages without stated repeated-run counts, seed protocols, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added temporal plots introduce no uncertainty estimates. The variational forecasting experiment already appears in v2.

E6.justification: Existing numerical entries are retained, but v4 adds substantial results for the new baseline, training variants, context/split study and temporal and qualitative diagnostics. For example, Table 10 newly reports joint-training averages of 21.79 PSNR and 0.0984 LPIPS versus 27.31 and 0.0467 for the original pipeline. These are additional experimental comparisons, not revised default scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical content of Equations 1–20 is retained, including adaptive weighting, the variational formulation and trajectory sampling. Replacing T_c/T_e with N_c/N_e where sample counts are intended aligns notation with existing definitions; no substantive assumptions, derivations or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same two-stage forecasting contribution, smoothness rationale, timestamp-independence argument and state-of-the-art claims. The headline 19.8% improvement and contribution-list metric improvements are unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 attributes the lack of general benefit from reprojection supervision to redundancy with the interpolation stage's image supervision. It interprets slower SSIM/LPIPS degradation as preservation of motion and appearance, and adds scene-dependent shorter-context guidance. Section 5's principal limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds an ODE-GS code-access link and a reproducibility statement reporting public implementation release. Existing architecture, hardware, optimizer, solver and regularization details are retained. New experiment descriptions specify random-camera sampling and keeping interpolation parameters trainable.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds five cited works covering evidential NeRF, additional dynamic Gaussian methods and ImageFlowNet, with a brief discussion of limited Neural ODE applications in 3D. It removes the earlier sentence emphasizing autoregressive positioning; the central relationship to existing reconstruction and extrapolation methods is retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and narrative order are retained. Targeted copyedits and notation clarifications accompany separate ablation and additional-experiment subsections, Appendix B.2.2, and new acknowledgments, ethics and reproducibility statements. Authorship and publication-header information also change.

P2.justification: v4 substantially expands visual evidence with three new tables, aggregate and ten scene-specific temporal plots, two no-ODE comparisons and a failure illustration. Existing visuals are retained; v2 Figure 5 becomes v4 Figure 6. Figure 2 moves and corrects 'Transformer Decoder' to 'Decoder'.

improvement.justification: The added reprojection and joint-training controls strengthen the justification for the existing design, while temporal and failure analyses make its behavior easier to assess. Reported code access improves reproducibility documentation. These are useful, limited gains: Table 11 lacks matched default-context results at most splits, restricting how broadly its improvements can be attributed to shorter context.
